about.title: Personal Injury Help in El Cerrito, California
about.longDescription: El Cerrito is a compact, walkable city, but its streets still carry a steady flow of regional traffic. In the most recent full year on record, the city logged 52 injury collisions, with 63 people hurt and 4 lives lost. Corridors like San Pablo Avenue, I-80, Route 123, and Potrero Avenue see the highest volume of reported collisions, and crash reports tend to cluster on Wednesday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m., a window when commuters, students, and shoppers all converge. If you were hurt in one of these incidents, you're likely dealing with pain, missed work, and a stack of paperwork you didn't ask for. LawProactive is a free service — we are not a law firm — that connects injured people in El Cerrito with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened. There's no cost to talk, and the attorneys we work with take cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there's a recovery. You don't have to figure out the legal side alone while you're trying to heal.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: California's Filing Deadline Is Real
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of injury to file most personal injury claims in California. Claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months, so waiting can cost you options.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life, unlike some other states.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no upfront legal fee. If there's no recovery, you owe no attorney fee for the work done.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after an injury in El Cerrito?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity, such as the city or county, was involved, the notice period can be as short as six months, so it's wise not to wait too long to look into it.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so being partly responsible doesn't automatically bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery may simply be reduced by the percentage of fault assigned to you.

items.question: Where do collisions tend to cluster in El Cerrito?
items.answer: Public crash records show higher collision counts along San Pablo Avenue, I-80, Route 123, and Potrero Avenue, with reports tending to peak on Wednesdays between 4 and 6 p.m. These are simply where more reported collisions have occurred, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is there a cap on what I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No. California does not cap non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in typical personal injury cases. This differs from some other states that limit these types of damages.

items.question: Does it cost anything to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No, connecting with an attorney through LawProactive is free, and LawProactive itself is not a law firm. The independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you receive a settlement or award.
